name: Teachable
tagline: Online course platform for creators to sell lessons, coaching, and digital products

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $39/month monthly and $29/month annually, with 7.5% transaction fee.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 5 published products; 1 admin; 100 active students; 5 imported students; 1 TB video storage

tiers.name: Builder
tiers.limits: 10 published products; 1 admin; 1,000 active students; 50 imported students; 1 TB video storage

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 50 published products; 5 admins; 5,000 active students; 1,000 imported students; 1 TB video storage

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.limits: Custom product, student, admin, support, and service limits

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual prices shown as effective monthly rates; about 22% lower)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Starter adds a 7.5% platform fee; payment processing is 2.9%+$0.30 US cards, 3.9%+$0.30 international cards, 3.49%+$0.49 US PayPal, and 4.99%+$0.49 international PayPal; $15 chargebacks; optional BackOffice adds 2%–2.8%. Student caps are removed only after $10,000 in direct annual sales.

verdictSummary: A basic course site with Stripe can be built, but student apps, tax/payments, course compliance, certificates, upsells, affiliates, and support make full parity hard.
coreLoopDIY: Build lessons/modules, student login, progress tracking, Stripe checkout, and gated course pages.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because course businesses need checkout, access, progress, and support to just work.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source learning management system; powerful but heavier than Teachable.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Courses, coaching-style communities, downloads and sales pages in one stack; you run the stack.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit has less mature coaching, reporting, marketing automation and creator-commerce polish, while the owner runs the infrastructure.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Frappe Learning
alternatives.desc: Courses, cohorts, assignments, quizzes, certificates and payments in a modern UI; coaching workflows are lighter.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.dataFormat: Course and user records in the Frappe/MariaDB site database; public/private site files on disk, while video lessons commonly embed external hosts
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe Learning is less creator-commerce and coaching focused than Teachable, and self-hosting means learning the Frappe stack.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting still needs Docker or a Frappe server, DNS/SSL and email; payments require separate gateway configuration

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: The most complete free LMS here, with the least creator-friendly first impression.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle's administration and learner interface are far less creator-friendly, and selling/coaching requires configuration or plugins.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

alternatives.name: Odoo Community
alternatives.desc: A website, course catalog, forums and payments inside an ERP; subtle it is not.

facts.install: Use Odoo's packaged installer, source install or Docker image, backed by PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Business and website records in PostgreSQL; uploaded attachments in Odoo's filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo's course experience is secondary to its ERP and lacks Teachable's creator-friendly coaching, authoring, marketing and student polish.
facts.setupBlocker: A production deployment needs PostgreSQL, workers/reverse proxy configuration, backups and ongoing administration of a very large suite

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: One hosted course, bookings, digital products and payments free; useful until your catalog becomes plural.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan's one-course ceiling and lighter assessment/creator-school tooling become the first major limit.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

alternatives.name: Tutor LMS
alternatives.desc: A full course shop inside WordPress; low GitHub stars, but current releases and more than 100,000 active installs.

facts.install: Install from WordPress Plugins → Add New, then run Tutor LMS's setup wizard
facts.dataFormat: Courses, enrollments and settings in the WordPress database; lesson media in the WordPress Media Library
facts.gapVsPaid: Tutor LMS depends on WordPress and key creator features such as subscriptions, certificates, assignments and drip content may require paid add-ons.
facts.setupBlocker: It first requires a maintained WordPress site, and subscriptions, certificates, assignments, drip content and several integrations sit outside the free core

notes: Important because course platforms are very tempting to DIY but full business flows are deep.
prompt:
Build me a single-course sales site to replace Teachable, for one course of mine. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS behind Caddy. Course content is Markdown
  in content/: one folder per module, one file per lesson, front matter points at an
  optional video file.
- Public landing page: course outline, price, and a Buy button that goes to Stripe
  Checkout (keys in .env). The Stripe webhook marks the buyer's email as enrolled.
- Student login by magic link: enter email, receive a signed login link via SMTP
  creds in .env. No passwords, no OAuth.
- Lesson pages are gated by enrollment; videos are MP4s served through the app with
  short-lived signed URLs so direct links expire.
- Progress: a mark-complete button per lesson and a progress bar per module, stored
  per student in SQLite.
- Receipts come from Stripe; do not build invoicing or tax logic (turn on Stripe Tax
  if needed).
- Out of scope: multiple courses, affiliates, certificates, upsells, coupons, and
  mobile apps. This sells and delivers one course.
- README: Stripe webhook setup, Caddy snippet, where videos live on disk, and an
  honest note that a VPS handles a small audience fine but a big launch needs real
  video hosting like Bunny.net.
